subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Sharma <ravi@astralogistics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Ravi --

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Customer-facing search and document summarization experiences are seeing variable p95 latency spikes during peak hours (~3pm-6pm PT).
- Current in-house infra struggles to maintain throughput for batched inference (search/query workloads) without high cost.
- Needs: consistent p95 latency SLA, predictable unit economics, and ability to deploy inside their VPC for PII-sensitive pipelines.

Goals you shared:
- P95 inference latency <= 200ms for 512-token average inference (search/rerank flows).
- Sustained throughput target of ~250-300 req/s for peak window with autoscaling to 600 req/s for bursts.
- Deployment on dedicated GPUs in their GCP VPC (no egress of request payloads to public infra).

Technical notes & initial feasibility:
- Model: you indicated preference for a 13B-class open model (mixed precision / int8 quantized) with fallback to a smaller 7B variant for burst handling.
- Suggested topology: 4x A100-style GPUs (dedicated pool) with shard + KV-cache strategy, autoscale to 8 GPUs for sustained higher throughput.
- Batching: aggressive micro-batching for throughput with latency-aware routing to keep p95 under target.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for conversational contexts and heavy re-use queries to reduce compute.

Attachments I promised to share: SLO worksheet (fill-in), architecture diagram, mutual action plan draft.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll send the SLO worksheet for you to fill with representative traffic patterns + top queries.
2) Our infra team will run an initial capacity estimate and share a recommended topology + cost ballpark by EOD tomorrow.
3) Schedule a PoC kickoff: 2-week PoC inside your VPC with canary traffic and SLO monitoring.

Would you confirm the p95/p99 targets above and the requested throughput numbers? If anything is off, I can update the workbook before you fill it.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ravi Sharma <ravi@astralogistics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Aditya --

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the targets: p95 <= 200ms for 512 tokens, p99 ideally < 500ms but we can discuss trade-offs. Throughput numbers are correct: 250-300 req/s sustained, with bursts to 600.

A few clarifications: we have a mix of short search queries (~64 tokens) and longer summarization requests (~400-700 tokens). The p95 SLA needs to hold across that mix, but search is the priority.

We need the PoC to run entirely inside our GCP VPC with customer-managed KMS. Also want to validate KV cache behaviour on warm vs cold cache conditions.

Happy to fill the worksheet -- please send. Can we target a PoC kickoff the week of Jun 21?

Best,
Ravi Sharma
Head of Search & AI
Astra Logistics

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Sharma <ravi@astralogistics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Thanks Ravi -- attaching the SLO worksheet and the architecture diagram. A few technical clarifications we discussed on the call: 

- Model sizing & quantization: we recommend a quantized 13B runtime (int8 or mixed int8/fp16) for the primary path. For burst handling, traffic can be routed to a quantized 7B variant; this keeps the user-facing latency within SLA while saving unit cost.
- Serving runtime: Redwood will run the inference runtime inside your VPC on dedicated GKE clusters (node pools backed by A100/80 GPUs). We use optimized kernels and continuous batching; the runtime exposes metrics for per-token latency, GPU utilization, and batch sizes.
- Autoscaling & topology: start with a 4-node pool (one model replica per GPU), target steady-state of 4 GPUs for baseline throughput, with policy-based autoscaling to 8 GPUs for sustained peaks. We recommend an additional small pool for warm cache instances to mitigate cold-start p95 spikes.
- Fallbacks & routing: policy-driven routing (latency-first for search queries, cost-first for background summarization) with transparent fallback to smaller model variants if a replica is saturated.
- Monitoring & SLO verification: we will instrument p50/p95/p99, token throughput, queue time, and cache hit rates. We will provide a Grafana dashboard and trace hooks for sample request tracing.

Next items I will deliver:
- Filled capacity estimate & cost ballpark (EOD tomorrow).
- Doc with PoC runbook and expected milestones.
- Mutual action plan draft (attached).

Looking at the PoC kickoff the week of Jun 21 -- does Wed Jun 23 at 10am PT work for you? If so I'll send a calendar invite and loop in Rishi (runtime lead) and Laura (customer success).

--
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLO-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-architecture-diagram.pdf, mutual-action-plan.docx

Thanks all -- looking forward to the PoC.
